= Local OpenSSL source

This directory contains the complete published `openssl-src` 300.6.1+3.6.3 package from the local Cargo registry source cache.
The package builds OpenSSL 3.6.3 and retains its upstream sources, build machinery and license notices.
The upstream package is https://crates.io/crates/openssl-src/300.6.1+3.6.3[openssl-src 300.6.1+3.6.3].
The OpenSSL source repository is https://github.com/openssl/openssl/tree/openssl-3.6.3[OpenSSL 3.6.3].

`UPSTREAM.sha256` records every original package file before local changes.
The manifest SHA-256 is `f513696ac0a80fb28ce9ac16d4ecbcf76b441973be5afd9a38365838fa1b9a49`.
The source cache contained no package archive checksum, so this manifest identifies the available source without asserting independent archive verification.
The workspace patch gives all OpenSSL consumers one source identity.
This source copy has not been compiled or executed during Phase 1.

The TLS context adds a borrowed signature library context through `SSL_CTX_set_signature_libctx` and `SSL_CTX_get0_signature_libctx`.
An omitted override preserves upstream behavior.
The setter must run before connections are created, and the supplied library context must outlive the TLS context and every connection.
CertificateVerify and TLS 1.2 ServerKeyExchange signatures use the override.
Protocol randomness, key generation, binder HMACs, cookie HMACs and record MACs retain the original TLS context.
These are all `EVP_DigestSignInit_ex` call sites in the pinned SSL source.

OpenSSL's signing setup fetches the signature implementation from the supplied library context and exports a preexisting key into that implementation's provider.
Keys loaded through native librdkafka options therefore use the signature override as well as keys decoded by the Java configuration adapter.
The Rust TLS owner retains both library contexts beyond native context destruction.
It does not rely on SSL context ex-data destruction, which occurs before native certificate keys are released.
Regression sources in `../../crates/kafka/src/tls/random` exercise TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 client certificates with RSA-PSS and ECDSA and retain the owners through connection teardown.

`X509_load_cert_crl_bio_ex` adds the existing PEM certificate/CRL file parser for a borrowed BIO.
Its result is the imported object count, or zero on failure; the caller retains BIO ownership.
The file entry point delegates to that parser after opening its original file BIO.
`SSL_CTX_use_certificate_chain_bio` loads a certificate and replaces its chain from a borrowed BIO using the same parser and password callbacks as the file entry point.
`OPENSSL_RTDB_MATERIAL_BIO` identifies these additive interfaces to the bundled librdkafka build.
Native Kafka snapshot and loader-order regression sources live in `../../crates/kafka/src/client/material/tests.rs`.
These changes do not alter the recorded upstream manifest and have not been compiled or executed during Phase 1.

`X509_STORE_CTX_verify_selected_chain` verifies a caller-selected leaf-first chain with a final trust anchor and borrowed Java self-issued facts.
The caller owns Java issuer matching, identifier parsing, critical-extension recognition, algorithm constraints and certificate policy.
The fresh context retains references to the original chain through normal context cleanup.
Its purpose is `ANY`, its native authentication level is zero, and its flags are limited to time checking, `PARTIAL_CHAIN` and `TRUSTED_FIRST`.
DANE, raw-public-key validation, revocation flags, proxy flags, strict-native validation and custom chain-verification functions are rejected at this boundary.
The ordinary OpenSSL verification entry points retain their existing behavior.

A passive call-local metadata owner duplicates non-anchor certificates and excludes only noncritical AKI/SKID extensions after the caller's Java parser has handled them.
This prevents OpenSSL's identifier-cache failures from overriding Java's noncritical-extension rules.
Metadata copies supply extension and name-constraint checks; original certificates supply every signature check, callback certificate and returned chain.
Neither shared X509 self-issued flags nor original certificate encodings are rewritten.
The final anchor is excluded from path-extension, name-constraint, date and signature checks.
Version-1/version-2 intermediates require Java self-issuance and immediate placement below the anchor.
Per-certificate metadata allocation is admitted before the native call and released after all copies are destroyed.
The regression sources are `../../crates/kafka/src/tls/validation/pkix/tests/selected_chain.rs`; they have not been compiled or executed during Phase 1.

`X509_set0_retained_owner`, `X509_CRL_set0_retained_owner` and `X509_STORE_set0_retained_owner` attach one passive resource owner to a native object's lifetime.
The setter transfers the opaque owner only on success, requires exclusive access before publication and rejects a second owner or a null destruction callback.
Native reference-counted aliases retain that same owner until the last reference is released.
Certificate and CRL owners run after their decoded fields, cached payload and heap object storage have been destroyed, including destruction through generic ASN.1 entry points.
Their inputs must be heap-allocated objects rather than embedded ASN.1 values.
Store owners run after lookup methods, cached references, pointer stacks and the store's own storage have been destroyed.
An independently retained certificate or CRL can outlive its store and carries its own owner until its final destruction.

The opt-in `ASN1_AFLG_FREE_FINAL` flag passes a zeroed `ASN1_FREE_ARG` to `ASN1_OP_FREE_POST`.
That callback may capture a destruction function and opaque argument; generic ASN.1 cleanup calls it after freeing the native object's storage.
The captured callback receives no pointer to the destroyed object and must not unwind through C.
Only X509 and X509_CRL opt into the flag in this source tree, and objects without retained owners use their existing cleanup path.
ASN.1 duplicates start without a retained owner; decoding into an existing object preserves its owner until that object's destruction.
These hooks provide lifetime ownership and do not admit new allocations made by duplication or subsequent mutation.
Custom CRL methods retain their existing cleanup behavior.
If a custom destruction callback aborts before cached payload cleanup, the retained owner is also left unreleased, keeping its admission while the skipped native allocations remain live.
The pinned built-in CRL method has no destruction callback and follows the complete payload cleanup path.
Native default/probe stores, inline inputs, nonregular files, arbitrary providers, and later handshake/session allocations remain independent admission qualifications.

`X509_STORE_set0_hash_dir_source` installs admitted lazy input on an existing hashed-directory lookup.

* The setter transfers one source owner only on success and closes further directory registration.
  It does not add a lookup, enumerate a directory or open a child path.
* The original subject-hash and numeric-suffix probes select each certificate or CRL file.
  A source callback supplies immutable admitted bytes to the certificate-only or CRL-only parser.
  The original file entry points use these same borrowed-BIO parser bodies without source callbacks.
* A decoded file owner attaches to each parsed object before cache insertion.
  Duplicate candidates release their temporary owners; objects imported before a later parse failure retain theirs.
* Metadata grants precede cache-object, pointer-capacity and CRL-suffix allocation.
  Grants commit only after publication or roll back after allocation cleanup.
  Each lookup also holds a temporary path-buffer grant until that buffer is freed.
* Admission denial returns zero from this lookup before cached-result selection and error clearing.
  Other lookup methods and already-cached store results retain their existing behavior.
  A distinct public budget error is not guaranteed when another result satisfies the lookup.
* The source owner is released through the store's final-cleanup hook.
  Independently retained certificates and CRLs keep their own decoded-file owners.

The Kafka binding and its regression sources live in `../../crates/kafka/src/client/material/directory`.
That binding documents its bounded-read behavior, conservative native decode allowance and remaining allocation qualifications.

`openssl/test/retained_owner_test.c` is a standalone native regression program.
Its process-local allocator hooks check that object, property, cached-extension, lookup and pointer-stack storage is freed before owner callbacks.
The cases cover generic ASN.1 cleanup, reference-counted aliases, failed ownership transfer, cached objects retained after store destruction and conservative owner retention after a custom CRL cleanup failure.
Deterministic Ed25519 fixtures also cover X509/CRL duplication with independent owners and successful decode into an existing object.
Malformed outer tags and empty sequences cover failed decode before and after `D2I_PRE`, including an alias that keeps the old object alive after the input pointer is cleared.
Malformed auxiliary certificate data covers `d2i_X509_AUX` returning failure while preserving an existing certificate and its owner.
The pinned paths are `crypto/asn1/a_dup.c:ASN1_item_dup`, `crypto/asn1/tasn_dec.c:asn1_item_ex_d2i_intern` and `crypto/x509/x_x509.c:d2i_X509_AUX`.

This package omits the upstream test harness sources.
The Cargo builder passes `no-tests` and invokes `make depend` followed by `make build_libs`; the root OpenSSL `build.info` excludes the entire test directory under `no-tests`.
Enabling the ordinary OpenSSL test targets would require omitted sources, so the standalone program is compiled directly against the configured library and generated headers.
The following Phase 2 workflow is scoped to a native Apple Silicon macOS host with Perl, Make and the Xcode command-line C toolchain, starting at the repository root.
It uses a separate build directory and the pinned `darwin64-arm64` target from `Configurations/10-main.conf`.
The program has its own `main`, requires the default Ed25519 implementation and does not link the missing test harness.

[source,shell]
----
rtdb_openssl_source="$PWD/rust/vendor/openssl-src/openssl"
rtdb_owner_build="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rtdb-retained-owner.XXXXXX")"
(
  set -e
  cd "$rtdb_owner_build"
  perl "$rtdb_openssl_source/Configure" darwin64-arm64 no-shared no-module no-tests no-comp no-zlib no-zlib-dynamic
  make depend
  make build_libs
  cc -arch arm64 -I"$rtdb_owner_build/include" -I"$rtdb_openssl_source/include" -I"$rtdb_openssl_source" \
    "$rtdb_openssl_source/test/retained_owner_test.c" "$rtdb_owner_build/libcrypto.a" \
    -o "$rtdb_owner_build/retained_owner_test"
  OPENSSL_CONF=/dev/null "$rtdb_owner_build/retained_owner_test"
)
----

Other platforms need their matching Configure target, compiler architecture and platform link dependencies.
This is a source-traced workflow rather than a successful build claim.
The hooks and regression source have been reviewed as source only, without compilation or execution during Phase 1.
